title: Hearty Flaky Polish Minari Pierogi
description: A traditional Polish dish featuring minari and a flaky puff pastry crust, perfect for a solo dinner, and diabetic friendly due to its balanced ingredients and portion control.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, and pepper, then add the cold butter and use a pastry blender to work it into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the water to the bowl, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together in a ball.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and roll it out to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
In a small bowl, mix the chopped minari with the sour cream and beaten egg.
Spoon the minari mixture onto one half of the dough, leaving a 1/2 inch border around the edges.
Fold the other half of the dough over the filling and press the edges together to seal the pierogi.
Use a fork to crimp the edges and create a decorative border.
Place the pierogi on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush the tops with a little bit of water.
Bake the pierogi in the preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until golden brown.
